summary: Fix the fleet map over-reporting cameras on a point asset (a junction, gate or pole). A point asset previously owned no floor-plan area at all, so the map computed its cameras as every camera on every appliance assigned to it (fleet_map.js's resolvedCamKeys fallback) - wrong whenever one mymatasan recorder feeds cameras in more than one place, which is the normal case (e.g. an NVR with cameras split across two buildings, assigned to a junction, made the junction claim all of them). Every point asset now gets one implicit, image-less 600x400 area (ISiteService.EnsurePointArea) so its cameras are pinned there like everywhere else: entities.HasPlans is renamed to HasDrawablePlan (same boolean, honest name - it answers whether there is a plan worth drawing/printing, never whether the site owns an area), the site inventory PDF prints a 'Cameras at this point' table instead of the old 'holds no floor plans' note, and the frontend now opens the same plan editor and drill-down for a point asset as every other kind (the separate appliance-chooser popup, rename-only dialog and camera-borrowing fallback are all removed). A boot-time backfill (EnsurePointAreas) idempotently repairs any point asset created before this existed.
compatibility: Backward compatible for existing installs. Every pre-existing point asset gets its implicit area created automatically on the next boot (idempotent, safe to run every boot, logged as a repaired count); no operator action needed and no site loses data. Existing buildings and outdoor areas are unaffected. The Go-side rename HasPlans -> HasDrawablePlan and the JS-side rename hasPlans -> hasDrawablePlan are internal API renames only (no wire-format or schema change).
